rationale: The Tarpa wind horn is the visual and rhythmic center of Warli community paintings; dancers form concentric spirals around the Tarpakar player.
Warli ritual wedding chauks prominently feature the sacred Mother Goddess Palghat and Kansari Devi as the protector of fertility and harvests.
Both traditions share the same animistic cosmological symbolism, visual geometry, and ceremonial invocation of the 52 forest deities.
source: Tribal Research and Training Institute Maharashtra (https://trti.maharashtra.gov.in/)

rationale: Ritual Suvasinis chant oral hymns and riddles in the native Varli dialect while applying white rice paste onto ochre walls.
Tarpa players lead the nightly ritual procession of mask-wearing deity impersonators through the village square.
The Simhastha Kumbh Mela ritual bath begins at the sacred Kushavarta pond located right beside the Trimbakeshwar shrine.
Pilgrims visiting the Trimbakeshwar and Godavari river banks customarily partake in traditional Nashik culinary fare.
Classic Paithani border motifs (peacocks, lotuses, parrots) draw direct stylistic inspiration from the stone carvings of Ajanta and Ellora.
